Your Role

We ship fast, and we intend to keep shipping fast. The consequence is that our system is outgrowing the amount of deliberate design that went into it. We run AI agents over customer documents in a domain where being wrong is expensive, and a lot of the load-bearing decisions about how those fit together are still implicit.

You will be making those decisions explicit and then making them hold. That means codifying golden paths, building the shared primitives and APIs that product engineers work on top of, owning the architecture of the system as a whole, and establishing what our reliability actually needs to be before an incident establishes it for us.

Platform at Cortea sits between software engineering, DevOps and SRE. Its customers are other engineers. This is not a DevOps role under a different name: you will spend more time in application code than in YAML, and the reason we want infrastructure experience is that we don't believe you can design a system well without being able to run it.

The bar we are hiring against is someone who has taken a system from nothing to production and owned it end to end. You picked the technology, argued the tradeoffs in writing, provisioned the infrastructure, and were responsible for it when it broke.


On AI

We use AI heavily and we want you to. What we are not looking for is someone who outsources their judgment to it.

The mental model of this system has to live in your head, not in a context window. Use agents to move quickly on implementation. Do the design, the reasoning and the writing yourself, and be able to defend every decision you ship.


What you'll do

Four areas, roughly in the order you will spend time on them. You won't work on all of them at once, but you should be open to any of them.

Product platform. Make the easiest way for product engineers to do something (the paved road, or golden path) also the most secure, reliable and scalable way by default. Build the shared primitives, libraries and APIs that hide complexity and carry our quality and observability standards with them. Own the architecture and the core stack: what gets standardized, what gets reused, and where the system should be in eighteen months.

Infrastructure, observability and reliability. Infrastructure as code by default, from cloud resources through to dashboards and alerts. Provision, run and tune our Kubernetes cluster and cloud footprint, and keep CI fast as the deploy rate grows. Define SLIs for the workloads that
matter, build SLOs on top of them, and make the alerting high-signal enough that people trust it. Drive down AI and infrastructure spend.

Security and compliance. Keep the internal foundations secure by default: IAM, dependency management, secrets. Own the authentication and authorization stack, including ReBAC models covering both humans and agents. Implement SOC 2 and ISO 27001 controls without taxing every future change.

AI dev tooling. Keep product engineers and their agents on the paved road by making sure the documentation and agent guidelines they need are in place. Shorten the path from design to implementation with standardized automations and development environments that stay close to production.


What this looks like in practice

  • A system of record for managing and distributing constantly evolving agent configurations, under strict auditability and tenant isolation requirements

  • The harnesses powering our AI agents, abstracting over use cases that change faster than the code

  • Centralized progress tracking that holds up across a growing number of parallel agent executions

  • Usage-based tenant billing with quotas and rate limiting across a growing set of products

  • SLIs for the background job system behind our agents (execution latency, AI spend, memory, CPU), then fixing the bottlenecks they expose at both the application and infrastructure level

  • A document pipeline handling dozens of file formats, very large spreadsheets and hundreds of parallel uploads, under a strong reliability requirement


You will fit into this role if you…

  • Have designed, built and operated distributed systems end to end, and enjoy understanding how every part interacts with the rest

  • Are strong at backend software engineering and at DevOps/SRE, and don't think of those as separate jobs

  • Write design docs, RFCs, ADRs, postmortems

  • Reach for simple, boring solutions first, can tell essential complexity from accidental, and know which corners are safe to cut and which ones compound

  • Can turn a hard problem on its head and find the alternative nobody proposed

Concretely, you have scaled Postgres or another relational transactional database under real load, run production Kubernetes, and built observability rather than inherited it: SLIs, SLOs, distributed tracing.

No one checks every box. If you have designed a system from scratch, run it in production, and can explain in writing why it is shaped the way it is, let's talk.


Nice-to-haves that are a plus:

  • Durable workflow orchestrators like Temporal, and background job and queue processing generally

  • Infrastructure for LLM-based products or agentic systems

  • Audit, finance, compliance, or another high-accuracy domain

  • Azure and/or GCP


This is probably not the right role if…

  • You would describe application code as someone else's responsibility. A large share of platform work here happens inside the product codebase.

  • Your answer to reliability is more process. We want guardrails, not gates.

  • You need a well-defined system to work in. Ours is not one yet, and shaping it is the job.


What you will get

  • You own the brand and shape how the product feels. Work face-to-face with experienced founders and learn directly from customer insights.

  • Real influence on strategy. In a small team of excellent engineers and operators with high autonomy, you will shape product direction. Best idea wins, regardless of seniority.

  • Fast, ambitious, and fun team. Decisions get made in hours, not weeks. Rapid experimentation is the default.

  • Meaningful equity and competitive salary. You are one of the first to build this, and you share in the upside.

  • A mission that matters. Building intelligent systems for a $200bn industry. From Berlin, with AI at the core.


Interview process

  • Second Call — Technical interview with Dan

  • Third Call — Deep dive into our culture with our Co-Founder Philipp

  • On-site Day (Berlin) — Meet the team and work on a real problem together

About AIOS

AIOS is building the world’s first full-stack AI doctor.

We’re at $400M ARR, growing from $10M/yr 12 months ago. We’re the world’s fastest growing AI doctor.

We’re faithfully serving >
column2:
150k/mo patients via Bolt Pharmacy, our main UK brand. We’re profitable.

Our strategy exists at the intersection of two strong theses:

  1. The AI doctor that wins will get to escape velocity using GLP-1s, the fastest growing consumer product in history.

  2. The $2T European healthcare market is overlooked by the most talented builders.

Our master plan:

  • Step 0 → $100M/yr by end of 2025: We went from $10M to $100M in 6 months serving the UK GLP-1 market.

  • Step 1 → $1B ARR by end of 2026: Over the last 12 months we've grown from 3k to 150k UK active GLP-1 patients. We’ll continue this growth curve to hit $1B ARR.

  • Step 2 → $10B ARR by end of 2028: Blitzscale Europe. We’ll be Europe’s largest GLP-1 provider.

  • Step 3 → $100B/yr by end of 2031: Get regulatory approval across Europe for our Full Autonomous Prescribing (FAP) system. Win contracts at scale with European payers to mass replace human labor. We’ll be the dominant full-stack AI doctor in Europe.

  • Step 4 → $1T/yr by end of 2035: With one line of code and zero human time, you can use AIOS to treat any patient globally with any medication.

In so doing, we’ll become the world’s first trillion-dollar healthcare company.

We’re a young, founder-led company. This is still Day 1 and all our work is ahead of us.

You can read more about working with us here: Working at AIOS

Being a Clinical Pharmacist at AIOS

We are building a world-class team.

At AIOS Tech (Bolt Pharmacy), we're building the world's first full-stack AI doctor. Right now it's akin to assisted self-driving (and improving every day), so humans are prescribing with AI assisting their workflows.

You'll join our growing team of Independent Prescribers, working through GLP-1 weight-management consultations day in, day out. You understand that a great patient experience means catching everything you need to prescribe safely and confidently first time - not sending someone back and forth for information you should have picked up on intake.

You'll assess each patient on their own merits: the comorbidity, the interacting medication, the case that needs a second look, and make the right call. You’ll never compromise on safety or accuracy.

You'll:

  • Deliver safe, evidence-based GLP-1 prescribing for every patient on your list

  • Take full ownership of the clinical quality, safety and accuracy of your own consultations and records

  • Flag anything that needs escalating—a red flag, a near miss, a protocol gap—clearly and quickly

  • Follow, and help sharpen, our clinical protocols as they evolve

This role is suited to a confident, forward-thinking prescriber with sound clinical judgement, excellent attention to detail, and a strong commitment to patient safety.

Great performance in this role means your patients are safe, your records hold up to audit, and you're working through a full, steady caseload without ever cutting corners. If you nail this role, you'll be a strong candidate for more senior clinical positions as we grow.

This is an ongoing contractor engagement - full-time (40h) preferred, part-time (20h+) available - fully remote/WFH or hybrid onsite in Blackburn.

You’ll report directly to your team lead.

You’ll also work most closely with:

  • Saim Dalvi (UK Clinical Lead)

  • Mobeen Nawaz (Interim Clinical Ops Lead)

  • Phuong Nguyen (Superintendent Pharmacist)

Key Responsibilities

  • Prescribing: Deliver safe, evidence-based GLP-1 prescribing for every patient you see — assessing suitability, comorbidities and contraindications before you write anything.

  • Consultations: Run detailed, efficient consultations that capture everything you need the first time, so patients aren't stuck in back-and-forth messiness.

  • Monitoring: Track treatment response and side effects across your caseload, and adjust care promptly and safely.

  • Escalation: Recognise what's outside your remit, and escalate red flags, near misses or complex cases to your Senior Clinician Team Lead quickly and clearly.

  • Documentation: Keep accurate, concise and contemporaneous clinical records that hold up to audit.

  • Governance: Contribute to clinical audits, incident learning and quality improvement when asked.

  • Collaboration: Work smoothly with customer support, operational and technology teams to keep the service safe and moving in service of our patient base.

Need to Have

  • Registration: GPhC-registered pharmacist with an Independent Prescriber (IP) annotation, held for at least 1 year.

  • GLP-1 Confidence: You've prescribed weight-management, GLP-1s or a closely related area — comorbidities and polypharmacy don't throw you off protocol.

  • Clinical Reasoning: You think clearly and quickly within a protocol-led service.

  • Safety Mindset: Patient safety and quality are non-negotiable for you. Red flags don't get past you.

  • Communication: Excellent written and verbal communication, including confident patient counselling.

  • Pace: Comfortable in a fast-paced, high-volume, protocol-led environment, and you don't let volume compromise accuracy.

  • Digital Literacy: Confident using electronic health records and remote consultation platforms.

  • Flexibility: Willing to support evening or weekend rotas when needed. With sufficient notice, you work the hours that our patients need you to work so they can be served without long wait times and unnecessary friction.

Nice to Have

  • Consultation Modes: Experience with asynchronous, telephone and/or video consultations.

  • Specialist Training: Additional training in obesity or weight management, such as SCOPE certification.

  • Postgraduate: A postgraduate clinical diploma or equivalent.

  • Complex Patients: Comfortable managing patients with diabetes, cardiovascular disease, renal impairment or polypharmacy.

  • Governance Experience: Some experience contributing to clinical audits, incident investigations or quality-improvement projects.

  • Protocols: Exposure to developing SOPs, clinical protocols or prescribing pathways.

  • Startup Pace: Experience working in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, ideally in the weight loss space.

  • Growth Mindset: An interest in eventually mentoring or supporting more junior colleagues as you grow with us.

  • Systems: Familiarity with clinical support and customer management systems.

Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

We're hiring a Senior People Operations Generalist to join our global People Operations team. You'll support our entire global population — onboarding, compliance, day-to-day HR questions — in true partnership with the rest of the team, with work divided by focus area rather than by region. You'll also take on our global compliance programs almost like a program manager: building them, maintaining them, and continuously improving how they run as we scale into new countries.

Based in Ireland or the UK, your experience and time zone will naturally make you the go-to person for EMEA and JAPAC coverage — making calls in real time while the rest of the team is offline. You'll report to our Senior Manager, People Operations and join a broader team of People Operations Generalists and Coordinators. This is a senior generalist role for someone who wants real ownership of a global function, with the backing of a larger team behind them.


What You'll Do

  • Support the end-to-end employee lifecycle for our global population: onboarding, changes, leaves, exits, and everything in between, as part of a global team with work divided by function and program rather than region alone

  • Own our global compliance programs like a program manager: build new processes, maintain and improve existing ones (right-to-work, statutory leave, GDPR/data protection, and more), and drive ongoing efficiency as we add countries

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for employees, managers, and external partners (brokers, EOR providers, government agencies) during EMEA/JAPAC hours, given your time zone and regional expertise

  • Partner with global payroll and EOR platforms (Deel, Remote, or similar) to manage country-specific new hire and offboarding requirements worldwide

  • Build and maintain SOPs so global processes are documented and don't depend on tribal knowledge

  • Represent the broader People Ops team on EMEA/JAPAC matters, using good judgment about what needs to wait for US hours and what doesn't

  • Partner cross-functionally with People Systems, Legal, IT, Payroll, and Workplace teams based in the US


What You Have

  • 4–6 years of HR/People Ops experience, ideally including time in a mature, multi-country organization

  • Experience running compliance like a program: building, maintaining, and improving processes over time, not just administering them

  • Strong, hands-on knowledge of employment law and compliance in at least one region outside the US — EMEA and/or JAPAC experience preferred, given the time zone value it brings

  • Working knowledge of GDPR and HR data protection requirements

  • Experience with HRIS/payroll platforms such as Workday, Deel, or Remote

  • A track record of working independently across a global, distributed team, with good instincts about when to escalate and when to just handle it

  • A strategic mindset with a strong inclination for program and project management

  • Excellent written communication, given the async nature of working across time zones

  • Comfort being the go-to point of contact for a region during your hours, and the confidence to represent the function externally

Not sure which Support role is right for you?

We’re hiring for both Product Support Specialist and Product Support Engineer roles.

  • Support Specialist owns cases and customer communication end-to-end. Troubleshoots complex issues by navigating internal tooling — audit logs, user experience testing, and API testing — to help customers reach successful outcomes.

  • Support Engineering serves as the escalation point between Support Specialists and Product Engineering. Owns integrations, supports data mapping and data migrations for customers, and resolves escalated tickets that don't require product code changes.

Please choose the role that best reflects your experience and interests rather than applying to both. If another Support role seems like a closer match, we’ll consider that in our review.

About the role

Support Engineering is the technical layer between frontline Support and Engineering. You’ll take on complex issues involving integrations, APIs, permissions, data, reporting, migrations, and workflows—using application behavior, logs, databases, and customer context to determine whether an issue can be resolved through Support or represents a product defect.

You’ll investigate issues end to end using tools such as Plain, GitHub, Datadog, databases, and the codebase. You won’t write the fix

You’ll also identify recurring issues, improve documentation and enablement, and partner with Product and Engineering on improvements. As Ashby’s first Support Engineer in EMEA, you’ll establish regional operating practices and handoff norms across European time zones while bringing EMEA customer patterns to a global team.

What you’ll own

  • Own complex technical issues from intake through resolution or escalation—investigating APIs, integrations, logs, data, configuration, and workflows to determine whether Support can resolve them or Engineering should be involved.

  • Set a high bar for complex technical investigations and ensure Engineering receives clear, actionable, well-validated product issues.

  • Build trusted working relationships with frontline Support, Engineering, Product, Customer Success, and customers.

  • Identify recurring problems and turn them into documentation, enablement, tooling, process improvements, or product feedback.

  • Partner with Product and Engineering on recurring product improvements by synthesizing customer patterns, validating defects, and sharing the technical context needed to choose between a product change, documentation, tooling, or process improvement.

  • Establish EMEA coverage, handoff, and operating practices across European time zones while bringing regional customer patterns to the global Support Engineering team.

  • Track and improve the outcomes that matter: resolution speed, escalation quality, fewer avoidable Engineering escalations, frontline self-sufficiency, reduced customer effort, and customer confidence.

You should apply if:

  • You’ve worked in a hands-on, customer-centric technical role where you independently investigate ambiguous issues involving APIs, integrations, logs, data, and application behavior.

  • You’re comfortable moving between customer conversations, APIs, logs, databases, product behavior, and code-level context to find root causes.

  • You can distinguish a configuration, data, documentation, or enablement issue from a true product defect—and explain your reasoning clearly.

  • You write precise investigations that others can quickly understand and act on, and communicate thoughtfully with technical and non-technical audiences across time zones.

  • You naturally look beyond the immediate ticket and improve the systems around it through documentation, enablement, tooling, or process design.

  • You want to be the first technical owner for EMEA and are energized by building regional structure within a global team.

  • You’re looking primarily for a high-volume support role centered on predefined troubleshooting steps, rather than open-ended technical investigation and ownership.

About B Lab
B Lab™ is the nonprofit behind Certified B Corporations™, a community of businesses that meet verified social, environmental, and governance standards. Together, our movement is working towards a more inclusive, equitable, and fair economic system.

Our history
B Lab began in 2006 with the idea that a different kind of economy was not only possible — it was necessary. Our founders Andrew Kassoy, Bart Houlahan, and Jay Coen Gilbert believed there was a better way to do business: better for workers, better for communities, and better for the planet.
column2: When our movement's first 81 Founding B&nbsp
column3: Corps signed the Declaration of Interdependence in 2007, they were not just proposing a better way of doing business. They were proposing a different definition altogether.&nbsp

column2: B Lab became known for certifying B Corporations™, companies that meet verified standards of social and environmental performance, accountability, and transparency. But we do much more than that. We help mobilize a global community of businesses committed to collective action on society's most critical challenges. In 2010, B Lab was part of successfully drafting and passing benefit corporation in Maryland, the first U.S. state to do so. This created a legal framework that allows companies to keep their values of care and community, not just shareholder value, at the forefront. Today, benefit corporation legislation is active in 52 jurisdictions around the world.

In 2024, leaders from across the network agreed to evolve into a more integrated organization that embodies interdependence. This next iteration of our global network will balance global coherence with local agency to achieve our vision of economic systems change. We are now building this future together.

Gestalten Sie Ihre Karriere mit uns!

Ein Kunstwerk um die Welt zu bringen ist Millimeterarbeit – die Infrastruktur dahinter ist es auch. Unsere Plattformen laufen auf einer Multi-Cloud-Umgebung aus Azure AKS und Hetzner Cloud, vollständig als Code beschrieben und über GitOps ausgerollt. Dieser Teil läuft zuverlässig und weitgehend selbsttragend – gut genug, dass wir denselben Ansatz jetzt auf die restliche, historisch gewachsene Infrastruktur ausweiten wollen, die bisher außerhalb unserer IaC liegt. Du wirst Teil unseres DevOps-Teams innerhalb von IT-OPS – einem der drei Bereiche unseres Business-Technology-Services-Teams (BTS) neben DPM und Dev, das wir gerade auf drei feste Mitarbeitende ausbauen – und prägst maßgeblich, wie diese Plattform technisch aussieht: durchdacht automatisiert, nachvollziehbar und so gebaut, dass Betrieb die Ausnahme bleibt und nicht zur Dauerbeschäftigung wird.


Ihre Aufgaben

Die Rolle ist bewusst breit – du arbeitest über den gesamten Stack und hast echten Gestaltungsspielraum:

  • Du betreibst und entwickelst unsere Multi-Cloud-Plattform weiter – Azure AKS und Hetzner Cloud (k3s) – und konsolidierst schrittweise unsere bestehende On-Prem-Umgebung.
  • Du entwickelst unsere Infrastructure-as-Code-Basis mit OpenTofu und Terragrunt weiter und automatisierst unsere VM- und On-Prem-Landschaft mit Ansible.
  • Du verantwortest unsere gesamte Delivery-Kette – von den GitLab-CI-Pipelines, Container-Builds und Quality-Gates bis zum GitOps-Rollout (ArgoCD, Kustomize, Helm) über Dev, Test, Acceptance und Produktion – samt der Tooling-Landschaft dahinter (GitLab, Registry, Runner).
  • Du baust unser Monitoring und unsere Observability weiter aus (Grafana, Prometheus/Thanos, Loki, Tempo).
  • Du verantwortest Secret-, Zertifikats- und Backup-Management (External Secrets Operator mit Azure KeyVault, cert-manager, Velero) sowie unsere Security-Werkzeuge (Trivy, Falco, OAuth2 Proxy) und die Identity-Anbindung über Entra ID.
  • Du betreust unser Netzwerk über beide Clouds hinweg – Firewalls (Azure, OPNsense), das Site-to-Site-VPN zwischen Azure und Hetzner sowie die Ingress-Schicht auf Basis der Gateway API (Envoy Gateway).
  • Du treibst Automatisierung und Standardisierung voran – damit wiederkehrender Betriebsaufwand verschwindet statt sich anzusammeln – und bringst nach und nach auch unsere bislang unverwaltete Legacy-Infrastruktur unter dieselben Standards und in unsere IaC.
  • KI gehört bei uns bereits zum Alltag: Änderungen durchlaufen automatisierte, KI-gestützte Reviews lokal, bevor sie das Remote erreichen. Du baust solche Workflows weiter aus und gestaltest unsere Infrastruktur bewusst KI-erweiterbar – bis hin zu Schnittstellen, über die agentische KI sicher mit unseren Systemen arbeiten kann.
  • Du bringst deine Erfahrung in die strategische Weiterentwicklung der Plattform ein – etwa zur sinnvollen Verteilung von Workloads zwischen Azure, Hetzner und on-prem.


Ihr Profil

Fachlich:

  • Mehrjährige Erfahrung mit Kubernetes im Produktivbetrieb, idealerweise über mehrere Cluster hinweg
  • Fundierte Erfahrung mit Infrastructure as Code (OpenTofu/Terraform, Terragrunt) und Konfigurationsmanagement mit Ansible
  • Praxis mit GitOps (ArgoCD/Flux, Kustomize/Helm) und CI/CD inklusive Container-Builds, idealerweise mit GitLab CI
  • Sicherer Umgang mit mindestens einer Public Cloud, Interesse an Multi-Cloud-Setups
  • Solides Netzwerk- und Security-Grundverständnis – Firewalls, VPN/IPsec, DNS und Ingress sowie Secret-Management und Identity/SSO
  • Erfahrung mit einem Observability-Stack rund um Prometheus und Grafana
  • Sichere Automatisierung mit Python (Bash selbstverständlich, Go von Vorteil)
  • Erfahrung darin, gewachsene Umgebungen zu konsolidieren und in einen wartbaren, automatisierten Zustand zu bringen
  • Sicherer Umgang mit agentischer KI im Arbeitsalltag und Interesse daran, Infrastruktur bewusst KI-erweiterbar zu gestalten
  • Zertifizierungen wie CKA oder Azure sind ein Plus, aber kein Muss – uns ist Praxiserfahrung wichtiger
Niemand bringt das alles mit – wichtiger als jeder einzelne Punkt sind Tiefe in den Kernbereichen (Kubernetes, IaC, eine Public Cloud) und die Neugier, dir den Rest zu erschließen.

Persönlich:
  • Du liebst es, dich tief in Systeme einzuarbeiten, Ursachen statt Symptome zu beheben und Probleme dauerhaft wegzuautomatisieren
  • Du denkst strategisch und behältst auch bei gewachsenen Systemen den Überblick
  • Du übernimmst gerne Verantwortung und gestaltest die technische Richtung unserer Plattform aktiv mit
  • Du gibst dein Wissen gerne weiter und förderst andere im Team
  • Du kommunizierst sicher auf Deutsch und Englisch (C1-Level), auch mit nicht-technischen Stakeholdern

investment-associate-intern-berlin-368996,Berliner Nachfolgewerk (BLNWRK),Investment Associate Intern,"

Zwei erfahrene Unternehmer bauen eine Nachfolgeholding für etablierte mittelständische Unternehmen auf, und du bist von Anfang an dabei: von den ersten Investments bis zu konkreten operativen Verbesserungen in unseren Beteiligungen.

Das Berliner Nachfolgewerk übernimmt profitable mittelständische Unternehmen in Nachfolgesituationen, vor allem aus den Bereichen B2B-Dienstleistungen und technische Services. Wir investieren ausschließlich eigenes Kapital und verfolgen eine langfristige Buy-and-Hold-Strategie. Die ersten beiden Übernahmen stehen kurz vor dem Abschluss.
Als Praktikant arbeitest du direkt mit uns, Felix und Milan.

Felix hat Arsipa seit 2020 durch Unternehmensnachfolgen und konsequente Digitalisierung zu einer Gruppe mit über 1.000 Mitarbeitenden aufgebaut. 2024 verkaufte er die Gruppe an Warburg Pincus und bleibt als Gesellschafter beteiligt.

Milan hat bei HomeToGo den Aufbau und die internationale Skalierung des Unternehmens mitgeprägt. Anschließend hat er Stellar Trust / Xentra mitgegründet, eine Softwarelösung für Ferienhausagenturen und Hotels.
Kennengelernt haben wir uns als Berater bei BCG.

Du arbeitest direkt an Analysen, Gesprächen und Entscheidungen mit und übernimmst schnell eigene Themen. Der operative Teil ist dabei kein Nebenschauplatz: Für uns beginnt die eigentliche Arbeit nach der Übernahme.
• Du identifizierst passende mittelständische Unternehmen und analysierst ihre Märkte, Geschäftsmodelle und Finanzzahlen.
• Du recherchierst Ansprechpartner, übernimmst Teile des Outreach und behältst das Follow-up im Blick.
• Du erstellst Unternehmensbewertungen, Financial Models und Investment Cases als Grundlage für unsere Investitionsentscheidungen.
• Du begleitest Due Diligence, Finanzierung und Transaktionsprozess und bereitest Gespräche mit Unternehmern, Managementteams und Finanzierungspartnern vor. Bei vielen bist du selbst dabei.
• Du übernimmst konkrete Projekte in unseren Beteiligungen, von der ersten Analyse bis zur Umsetzung mit den Teams vor Ort.
• Du analysierst Vertriebs-, Kosten- und Prozessdaten und entwickelst daraus Maßnahmen, die anschließend umgesetzt werden.
• Gemeinsam mit den Teams entwickelst du Vertrieb, Reporting und interne Abläufe weiter.
• Du findest die Stellen, an denen Software, Daten und KI-gestützte Automatisierung einen echten Unterschied machen, und setzt passende Lösungen mit um.
• Du gestaltest den weiteren Aufbau von BLNWRK und unserer internen Strukturen mit.
• Du verbesserst unsere Prozesse, Tools und Datenbanken dort, wo du Potenzial siehst.
• Du studierst BWL, VWL, Wirtschaftsingenieurwesen, Wirtschaftsinformatik oder etwas Vergleichbares.
• Du arbeitest analytisch und verlierst auch bei komplexen Themen nicht den Überblick.
• Du hast ein gutes Gespür für Zahlen und ein echtes Interesse an unternehmerischen Zusammenhängen.
• Du bist pragmatisch und hast keine Berührungsangst davor, in einer Beteiligung vor Ort mit anzupacken.
• Du beherrschst Excel und PowerPoint sicher. Erfahrung mit SQL, Python oder KI-gestützter Automatisierung ist ein klares Plus.
• Du hast bereits erste praktische Erfahrung gesammelt, etwa in Beratung, Investment Banking, Private Equity, einem Start-up oder einem mittelständischen Unternehmen.

Du begeisterst dich für Datenanalyse und möchtest deine Fähigkeiten in einem dynamischen, praxisnahen Umfeld einsetzen? Dann werde Teil unseres Teams als Business Analytics Intern und unterstütze uns dabei, datenbasierte Entscheidungen zu treffen und unsere Geschäftsprozesse weiterzuentwickeln.

Dabei arbeitest du an der Schnittstelle von Energiewirtschaft, Datenanalyse und Vertrieb und hilfst uns, das wirtschaftliche Potenzial von Energieanlagen und innovativen Versorgungslösungen zu bewerten.

Business Analytics Intern

Festanstellung, Vollzeit · Berlin (HQ)

Deine Mission

Du begeisterst dich für Datenanalyse und möchtest deine Fähigkeiten in einem dynamischen, praxisnahen Umfeld einsetzen? Dann werde Teil unseres Teams als Business Analytics Intern und unterstütze uns dabei, datenbasierte Entscheidungen zu treffen und unsere Geschäftsprozesse weiterzuentwickeln.

In dieser Rolle automatisierst du Workflows, analysierst kommerzielle Kennzahlen und gewinnst wertvolle Erkenntnisse aus komplexen Daten. Außerdem arbeitest du an Energiesimulationen und entwickelst gemeinsam mit unserem Team Python-basierte Tools weiter – beispielsweise für die Simulation von Batteriespeichern oder die Bewertung innovativer Energieversorgungslösungen.

Das Praktikum bietet dir umfassende praktische Erfahrungen an der Schnittstelle von Analytics und Energiewirtschaft. Du erhältst Einblicke in ein schnelllebiges Umfeld und hast die Möglichkeit, im Anschluss in eine Werkstudent:innenrolle zu wechseln.

Wenn du Lust hast, Verantwortung zu übernehmen, datenbasierte Lösungen zu entwickeln und die Energiewende aktiv mitzugestalten, freuen wir uns auf deine Bewerbung!

Das Team

Du wirst Teil des Commercial-Teams und unterstützt unsere Go-to-Market-Aktivitäten mit Potenzialanalysen, Energiesimulationen und kommerziellen Auswertungen. Dabei arbeitest du an der Schnittstelle von Energiewirtschaft, Datenanalyse und Vertrieb und hilfst uns, das wirtschaftliche Potenzial von Energieanlagen und innovativen Versorgungslösungen zu bewerten.

Deine Projekte

Profitabilitätsanalysen und Energiedatenmodellierung

  • Du führst Wirtschaftlichkeitsberechnungen für Industriekund:innen durch, bereitest Energiedaten auf und entwickelst Modelle zur Bewertung verschiedener Energieversorgungslösungen.

Workflow-Automatisierung und Prozessoptimierung

  • Du identifizierst wiederkehrende Abläufe und entwickelst datenbasierte Automatisierungslösungen, die unsere internen Prozesse effizienter und skalierbarer machen.

Energiesimulationen und Batteriesteuerung

  • Du nutzt Python-basierte Simulationen für energiewirtschaftliche Anwendungsfälle und entwickelst sie weiter – beispielsweise zur intelligenten Steuerung von Batteriespeichern oder zur Bewertung innovativer Versorgungslösungen.

Datenanalyse und Visualisierung

  • Du analysierst Energie-, Preis- und kommerzielle Daten, identifizierst relevante Zusammenhänge und bereitest deine Erkenntnisse in aussagekräftigen Visualisierungen für Fallstudien, die Website, Vertriebsaktivitäten und interne Stakeholder auf.

Deine Verantwortlichkeiten

  • Datenanalyse und Wirtschaftlichkeitsberechnungen: Du analysierst umfangreiche Energie- und Preisdaten unserer Kund:innen und führst mithilfe unserer Simulationstools detaillierte Wirtschaftlichkeitsberechnungen für verschiedene Energieversorgungslösungen durch.

  • Simulationen und Angebotserstellung: Du wertest Simulationsergebnisse aus und unterstützt das Team dabei, maßgeschneiderte und datenbasierte Angebote für potenzielle Kund:innen zu entwickeln – beispielsweise für Batteriespeicher und innovative Versorgungslösungen.

Gleichzeitig entwickelst du deine Kenntnisse in Data Science, Prozessautomatisierung und Softwareentwicklung kontinuierlich weiter.

Wen wir suchen

  • Du bist derzeit in einem Bachelor- oder Masterstudiengang in Data Science, Informatik, Statistik, Mathematik, Physik, Ingenieurwissenschaften, Wirtschaftswissenschaften oder einem verwandten Fachbereich eingeschrieben.

Nach sechs Wochen: Onboarding

  • Du verstehst trawas Geschäftsmodell, unsere Produkte, Kund:innen und zentrale energiewirtschaftliche Zusammenhänge.

  • Du bist mit unseren Datenstrukturen, Simulationstools und Analyseprozessen vertraut und kannst erste Analysen mit Unterstützung des Teams eigenständig durchführen.

Im dritten Monat: Ramp-up

  • Du setzt eigenständig ein Projekt in einem der Bereiche Datenanalyse, Workflow-Automatisierung, Profitabilitätsanalyse oder Energiesimulation um.

  • Du unterstützt die Erstellung kundenindividueller Angebote, indem du Energie-, Preis- und kommerzielle Daten analysierst und Simulationsergebnisse in klare Handlungsempfehlungen übersetzt.

Warum trawa?

Gestalte mit uns die Zukunft der Energiewirtschaft und treibe eigenverantwortlich Projekte voran, die echten Einfluss auf unsere Produkte, unsere Kund:innen und die Umwelt haben. Das erwartet dich bei uns:

  • Persönliche Entwicklung: Du arbeitest mit modernen Technologien und lernst von erfahrenen Expert:innen aus der Branche.

  • Vielfalt und Inklusion: Bei uns sind alle willkommen. Wir setzen uns für einen inklusiven Arbeitsplatz ein, der Vielfalt wertschätzt. Deshalb ermutigen wir Menschen unabhängig von Geschlecht, Alter, sexueller Orientierung, ethnischer Herkunft sowie körperlicher oder neurodiverser Vielfalt zur Bewerbung.

Über trawa

Willkommen im trawa-Universum! Wir haben es uns zur Aufgabe gemacht, das grüne Energieversorgungsunternehmen der Zukunft von Grund auf aufzubauen.

Wie machen wir das? Wir schaffen direkten Zugang zu erneuerbarer Energie für B2B-Industrieunternehmen. Wir entwickeln Software und Technologie, um die Volatilität des Energiemarkts zu bewältigen, und professionalisieren die Energiebeschaffung auf der Käuferseite.

The Ethereum Foundation

The Ethereum Foundation (EF) is a global non-profit organization dedicated to supporting Ethereum. Our mission is to help Ethereum remain secure, decentralized, and resilient over the long term by supporting critical protocol work and the broader ecosystem.

The role

The Protocol Security team helps prevent vulnerabilities from reaching Ethereum mainnet.

We work across the execution layer, consensus layer, networking, specifications, testing, and client implementations to identify security issues before they become production incidents. Our work combines deep protocol knowledge with security research, manual review, fuzzing, AI-assisted analysis, audits, and coordinated disclosure.

We're looking for engineers who already understand Ethereum deeply.

The strongest candidates are already active in Ethereum protocol development. Ideally you have deep experience with the execution layer, consensus layer, specifications, testing infrastructure, or other protocol-critical components.

What you'll work on

Examples include:

  • AI-assisted security research and automated bug discovery.

  • Reviewing upcoming hardforks.

  • Finding vulnerabilities across Ethereum protocol implementations.

  • Building and improving fuzzers.

  • Improving the team's automation and security tooling.

  • Manual security review of Ethereum protocol changes.

  • Working closely with Protocol DevOps, Specifications, researchers, and protocol implementers.

  • Coordinating responsible disclosure.

  • Supporting external audits and audit competitions.

What we're looking for

We're primarily looking for people with deep Ethereum protocol experience.

Ideal backgrounds include:

  • Deep familiarity with the execution layer or consensus layer.

  • Deep familiarity with EL or CL specifications.

  • Experience implementing or reviewing protocol changes.

  • Strong understanding of Ethereum networking, consensus, or execution internals.

Security experience should include one or more of:

  • AI-assisted security workflows.

  • Protocol security research.

  • Fuzzing.

  • Vulnerability research.

  • Manual application security review.

  • Building security tooling.

Languages commonly used include Go, Rust, Java, C#, Nim, and Python.

We're much less concerned with a specific number of years than with demonstrated technical depth.

Your Impact

We're strong at landing new customers. Now we need to get excellent at growing them.

Expanding within the customer base is one of Tacto's biggest growth levers, and we're building it out for the long term. Most mature B2B companies generate 50%+ of their revenue from existing customers - we want to capture more of that potential, and we're strengthening the team to get there. As Account Manager, you'll be a driving force behind our expansion motion: identifying and closing upsells, cross-sells, and strategic price increases across our customer base, and helping build and sharpen the playbook as we scale it. You'll work between Sales, Customer Value, and Product, spotting growth opportunities and turning them into revenue. This is your chance to build and grow a crucial commercial function at one of Europe's fastest growing industrial AI companies.

Your Impact

Procurement is over 50% of revenue for industrial companies and their biggest lever for profitability. The hard part is not the software, it is that every single customer's reality is different: a different ERP, a different data model, decades of undocumented process. Generic platforms stall exactly there, and that gap is where most enterprise AI value quietly dies.

Forward Deployed Engineering is how we close it: engineers who sit inside the customer's environment, build in their data, and turn what they learn into product. This function does not exist at Tacto yet. You will build the motion from the start, collaborating with Product, and discover what Forward Deployed Engineering means for Tacto, figuring out how much value we can generate for leading industrials.

Your Tasks

  • Build the function. Charter, operating model, quality bar, metrics. Bring this function to the next level.

  • Hire the right talent. The team is there to grow. Hire exceptional Forward Deployed Engineers and build your own high performing team.

  • Own how we engage customers. Design and establish the processes for how engineers scope, embed, build, and hand over. This is the core of the role, not an afterthought to the technical work.

  • Build, hands-on, in customer environments. Agents, pipelines, custom logic on top of our platform, in real production data. You lead by shipping.

  • Turn one-offs into product. Work directly with Product and Engineering to convert what you build at the edge into platform capability. An FDE org that productises nothing is just an expensive consultancy, and you will make sure we never become one.

  • Lead the first FDEs. Find the rare people who are excellent engineers and credible in front of a Head of IT. Set the standard by being it.

  • Own the hardest customer rooms. Lead escalations with Heads of Procurement and IT and be the senior presence customers trust.

  • Be AI-native. Use AI to change what the function is capable of, then measure it, then build it into how the team works.

Your Profile

  • 5+ years building software close to customers: forward deployed or deployment-style engineering, technical program leadership in a product company, or an engineering-heavy path through top-tier consulting at Manager level or above.

  • You write code and you want to keep writing it. Python and SQL at working level, comfortable with data pipelines and integration architecture.

  • 1+ years leading engineers, or you have built something from zero and had people follow you into it.

  • Zero-to-one operator. You are comfortable when the process does not exist yet, and you write it down instead of holding it in your head.

  • Product instinct. You can tell a one-off from a pattern and you will argue the case either way.

Why This Role is Awesome

Do this well for 12 to 18 months and you own one of Tacto's core technical organisations, with a direct line into the product roadmap and a hand in how leading global industrials adopts AI.

Your Impact

Procurement is the single biggest cost position for industrial companies, often 60-70% of revenue. Tacto brings AI to strategic procurement so teams can move faster, become more resilient and unlock savings at scale. However, winning a customer takes more than a good platform. It takes a business case that convinces the C-level (primarily CEO and CFO).

As our Value Engineer, you own exactly that. You quantify what Tacto is worth to a specific customer, prove it with their own data, and present it to the executives who sign. As the first Value Engineer in a dedicated segment, you are perfectly positioned to shape this function and maximize its impact.

It's a hands-on, high-trust role at the center of our deals, ideal for someone who wants to combine procurement expertise, analytical depth, and the C-suite room in one role.

Your Tasks

  • Make our AI tangible: Tacto's AI runs billions of spend and finds savings customers didn't know existed. Your job is to demonstrate that with the customer's own data: make sure our solution fits their needs, they recognize the value, blockers are resolved, and the path to a successful implementation is set.

  • Build the Business Case: Construct ROI analyses that stand up to C-level readout standards: real customer data, defensible baselines, scenarios and sensitivities. Your numbers directly shape whether deals are won.

  • Bring the Procurement Expertise: You are the person with in-depth knowledge of categories, procurement organizations and processes. Dig through spend data for price anomalies, bundling opportunities and supplier alternatives, and turn insights into a value story.

  • Own the C-Suite: Lead executive meetings with CEOs, CFOs and managing directors of industrial companies. You present, justify and land the case.

  • Work as a Deal Team: You team up with an Account Executive on every deal: the AE owns the program and the customer relationship, you own the value. Together you form the deal team that gets customers over the line.

  • Shape the Product: Be the voice of sales and customers towards the product team. Channel feedback, discuss roadmap trade-offs from a customer perspective, and know every Tacto module deep enough to demo solo.

Your Profile

  • You've worked in procurement or procurement consulting and know categories, negotiations, supplier management and procurement organizations from the inside

  • You're analytically sharp: you find the story in messy spend data and turn it into ROI calculations a C-level trusts

  • You're at your best in front of C-level audiences and stay sharp when they push back

  • You learn products fast and deep, and thrive diving into in-depth technical demos

  • You take ownership across teams (Sales, Solution Engineering, Product, Customer Value) and drive deals forward without being asked

  • You use AI tools to move faster than people expect

  • Fluent in German and English (our buyers decide in German)

Why This Role is Awesome

Tacto is already the leading AI solution for procurement, running billions of € of spend every month, increasing resilience and saving millions in measurable, tangible spend each week. For customer leads, that value can feel abstract at first. Your job is to make it tangible: demonstrate the capabilities of our solution with the customer's own data, and create the trust that convinces them to buy. You'll work closely with the sales team and Tacto's senior leadership, shape the future product roadmap and development, and as the first Value Engineer in your segment you build the function to maximize its impact.

What This Role Is and Isn't

Meet DeepL

DeepL is a global AI product and research company focused on building secure, intelligent solutions to complex business problems. Over 200,000 business customers and millions of individuals across 228 global markets today trust DeepL's Language AI platform for human-like translation, improved writing and real-time voice translation.
Founded in 2017 by CEO Jaroslaw “Jarek” Kutylowski, DeepL now has around 1,000 passionate employees and is supported by world-renowned investors including Benchmark, IVP, and Index Ventures.

Our goal is to become the global leader in trusted, intelligent AI technology, building products that drive better communication, foster connections, and create a meaningful impact. To achieve this, we need talented people like you to join our journey. If you’re ready to shape the future of AI and grow your career in a fast-moving, purpose-driven environment, DeepL is your next destination.

What sets us apart

What sets us apart is our blend of cutting-edge AI technology, meaningful work, and a culture where people truly thrive. We’re a team of innovators, researchers, and creators driven by a shared purpose to unlock human potential by making work simpler, smarter, and more connected.

When we share what it’s like to work at DeepL, the reactions are overwhelmingly positive. This might be because of our technology that helps millions of people and businesses communicate and work better every day, or because of the trust, curiosity, and care that shape our culture.

What we know for sure is this: being part of DeepL means joining a team dedicated to innovation, growth, and well-being. Discover more about life at DeepL onLinkedIn,Instagram, and our Blog.

How you will contribute to DeepL's success

  • Lead, inspire, and set the strategic vision for the Enterprise Sales team in Germany and contribute to the broader DeepL sales organisation

  • Build and grow a high-performing team through thoughtful hiring, structured onboarding, ongoing coaching, and professional development of Account Executives

  • Be the driving force behind scaling the team and the business — creating the processes, playbooks, and culture that enable sustainable, long-term growth

  • Own your team's performance targets and cultivate an environment where every AE can do their best work

  • Collaborate closely with Sales Development, Solution Consulting, Customer Success, Product, and Marketing to align priorities and maximize collective impact

  • Develop and maintain a deep understanding of DeepL's product and competitive landscape to support your team with confidence

  • Build, track, and analyse sales pipelines and buying trends, using insights to continuously improve how we work

  • Report predictably and accurately to senior leadership on progress and challenges, including regular forecasting

  • Establish scalable policies and processes that set the team — and DeepL's Enterprise revenue — up for success

  • Roll up your sleeves when it matters: you lead by example and show up for your team and customers

Product Designer at Aios Medical — Remote, $90k-$150k/yr inc equity

About AIOS

AIOS is building the world’s first full-stack AI doctor.
We’re at $350M ARR, growing from $10M/yr 12 months ago. We’re the world’s fastest growing AI doctor.
We’re faithfully serving >
column2:
150k/mo patients via Bolt Pharmacy, our main UK brand. We’re profitable.
Our strategy exists at the intersection of two strong theses:

  1. The AI doctor that wins will get to escape velocity using GLP-1s, the fastest growing consumer product in history.

  2. The $2T European healthcare market is overlooked by the most talented builders.

Our master plan:

  • Step 0 → $100M/yr by end of 2025: We went from $10M to $100M in 6 months serving the UK GLP-1 market.

  • Step 1 → $1B ARR by end of 2026: Over the last 12 months we’ve grown from 3k to 150k UK active GLP-1 patients. We’ll continue this growth curve to hit $1B ARR.

  • Step 2 → $10B ARR by end of 2028: Blitzscale Europe. We’ll be Europe’s largest GLP-1 provider.

  • Step 3 → $100B/yr by end of 2031: Get regulatory approval across Europe for our Full Autonomous Prescribing (FAP) system. Win contracts at scale with European payers to mass replace human labor. We’ll be the dominant full-stack AI doctor in Europe.

  • Step 4 → $1T/yr by end of 2035: With one line of code and zero human time, you can use AIOS to treat any patient globally with any medication.

In so doing, we’ll become the world’s first trillion-dollar healthcare company.
We’re a young, founder-led company. This is still Day 1 and all our work is ahead of us.

You can read more about working with us here:Working at AIOS

Being a Product Designer at AIOS

We are building a world-class team.

You’ll be taking on a senior, high-ownership role in product design at Aios Medical. We have multiple roles in the team across our clinical software and customer facing mobile app.

You’ll be stepping into a product that has grown fast and needs stronger design leadership, judgment, and structure.

Some of this work is visible and polished. Some of it is messy and internal. You’ll own projects end-to-end. That means taking loosely defined problems, talking to the right people, understanding workflows and constraints, and shipping solutions you can stand behind. We’re looking for someone who can run with a problem independently and be trusted to get it over the line.

The work often sits at the intersection of user needs, business goals, and real constraints. You might be working with engineers on a customer app flow, untangling a complex internal workflow that’s slowing teams down, reviewing CX tickets to understand where users are breaking, or defending a design decision.

You’ll report directly to our Head of Product Design (Ryan Wu) and work closely with our Head of Product (Ben Dowdle). You’ll also work alongside the rest of our Product and Design org, as well as our engineering and CX teams. You’ll be superb at collaborating and moving fast.

This is a full-time, remote role. We’re async-friendly and flexible with hours, but overlap with European and US time zones is expected.

Key responsibilities

  • Design ownership: You take ownership of design work across products and run projects independently, from problem definition to shipped solution.

  • Customer apps: You design and improve customer-facing web and mobile app experiences. Mobile app work is a major focus area.

  • Internal tools &
column3:
workflows: You work on internal products used by clinical, ops, enrolment, and CX teams, focusing on workflow, usability, and efficiency.

  • Complex problem solving: You work on products with real commercial and regulatory constraints. You understand that not everything can be changed freely.

  • Business &
column4:
user understanding: You start from the business problem and the user need. You can clearly explain what problem you were solving and why.

  • End-to-end project ownership: You lead projects independently, including discovery, talking to users or internal teams, defining the solution, and shipping it.

  • Clear communication: You can articulate your thinking, defend decisions, and hold your ground in discussions with strong opinions.

  • Hands-on leadership: You’re comfortable being senior, helping shape how design works, and supporting other designers as the team grows, without stepping away from hands-on work.

    • Need to have

    Experience: You’ve spent 3+ years designing digital products across web or mobile, including customer-facing mobile apps or internal tooling. What matters is that you’ve designed real products used by real people.

    Robust Portfolio: Your portfolio shows real product work that shows off your design taste. We want to see the problem, the rules you had to work within, and the impact of your decisions - including polished screens of the output.

    Ownership: You take loosely defined problems and run with them. You figure out what needs to be done, who to talk to, and how to move a project from idea to shipped solution. You don’t need constant direction, and you don’t get stuck in endless exploration.

    Craft: You care about clarity and usability more than surface-level polish. You can work within fixed requirements, technical limitations, and existing systems, and still make meaningful improvements.

    Clear thinking &
column5:
communication: You can clearly explain what problem you were solving, why certain decisions were made, and what tradeoffs were involved. You’re comfortable defending your work and navigating discussions with strong opinions.

Nice to have

Formal or equivalent design training: You’ve studied design, computer science, or a related field - or you’ve built the same depth of thinking through real product work.

Working in regulated and complex products: You don’t need experience in healthcare specifically. What matters is that you’ve worked on products where design decisions are shaped by regulation, compliance, legal requirements, or strong business rules. You understand that some copy, flows, or elements can’t simply be removed or redesigned, and that good design often means improving clarity and usability within those realities

Design that gets built: You’re comfortable working with engineers and thinking through implementation details. You understand how design decisions show up in real code and systems.

Our cultural standards

We aim to make this your life’s work. This should be the most challenging, most rewarding role of your life. Accordingly, these are the core cultural standards to which we hold ourselves &
column6:
our team-members:

  1. Belief in the mission: We will have served 100 million patients by the end of 2035 and we transform the life of most patients who join. We have a lot of work to do. We are obsessed with our patients and are dedicated to the mission.

  2. Unwavering integrity: We are at the frontier, so we often live in ambiguity with no trodden path. When we can’t look to others for guidance, we must maintain impeccable ethics and unwavering integrity.

  3. Only the paranoid survive: Bad sh*t is coming. By joining us, you’re choosing to sail straight towards the storms with unhesitating conviction. However much we’ve already done, however far we’ve already come — it’s still Day 1 and all our work is ahead of us.

  4. If we’re average we fail: We are only interested in “insanely great”, a focus on the quality of our execution that in everyday life would be considered pathological. We have a dedication to excellence and reject incompetence.

  5. Commitment to candor: That which can be destroyed by the truth should be. You get full transparency from the company and the company expects full transparency from you. We never say anything about someone that we wouldn’t say to them directly. We give feedback with love and do not need to protect people from fleeting physical sensations.

  6. A maniacal sense of urgency: We execute at an intensity that most people think is impossible. Speed is critical and we need things done yesterday. We all work very hard and in such a competitive world there really is no other way to win.

  7. Enduring frugality: We are frugal. We hate being wasteful and we are anti-luxury. A culture of cheapness keeps us young. We spend our cash wisely &
column7:

Your Mission

As our ICT Outsourcing Manager, you strengthen how lemon.markets manages and governs external technology services, outsourcing arrangements, and third-party risk in a regulated environment. Sitting at the intersection of Technology, Compliance, Operations, and partner governance, this role helps ensure that our provider landscape is transparent, well-documented, risk-based, and operationally under control. Over the next 6–12 months, your main focus will be to professionalise and stabilise our third-party management setup across external providers, tied agents, and intra-group outsourcing relationships. You will help turn recurring governance work into reliable operating routines, from assessments and reporting to escalations and evidence gathering. This is a hands-on role with real impact, especially for someone who enjoys creating structure, driving follow-up, and continuously improving operational processes.

In this role you will:

  • Act as the first line competence centre for ICT outsourcing and third-party governance topics, working across Technology, Compliance, Operations, business owners, and external partners to ensure risks and responsibilities are transparent and well managed.

  • Own the operational execution of our ICT third-party and outsourcing governance framework across external providers, tied agents, and intra-group outsourcing arrangements, so that key relationships are assessed, documented, and monitored in line with regulatory expectations.

  • Drive risk assessments, due diligence processes, and recurring reviews for new and existing third parties, coordinating relevant stakeholders and turning findings into clear actions, decisions, and follow-ups.

  • Maintain and improve the outsourcing register, governance documentation, and supporting evidence base, creating the level of clarity and traceability needed for internal stakeholders, auditors, regulators, and partners.

  • Prepare, structure, and run governance and review routines, including reporting, meeting preparation, escalation tracking, and action follow-up, to make third-party oversight more consistent, measurable, and decision-useful.

  • Identify and advance process improvements, standardisation opportunities, and selective AI-supported automation in recurring third-party management workflows, helping the function become more scalable and effective over time.

You’ll be successful in this role if you:

  • Bring hands-on experience in ICT outsourcing, third-party management, vendor risk, IT governance, compliance-related operations, or a similar function in a regulated environment.

  • Have a solid understanding of how external providers and outsourcing relationships are governed, documented, and monitored from a risk and compliance perspective.

  • Are comfortable working with risk assessments, service levels, control evidence, recurring reporting, and cross-functional governance routines.

  • Have enough technical affinity to understand IT services, security-related topics, incidents, and operational dependencies without needing to be a security engineer.

  • Work in a highly structured and reliable way, with strong follow-up discipline, good judgment, and the ability to keep multiple stakeholders aligned.

  • Communicate confidently in German and English, and enjoy making complex governance topics clear, practical, and actionable.

senior-software-engineer-setrade-munich-226660,VISPIRON GmbH,Senior Software Engineer (m/w/d) - SEtrade,"

Strom lässt sich nicht auf Halde legen. Erzeugung und Verbrauch müssen sich in jeder Sekunde ausgleichen, sonst kippt die Netzfrequenz. Das ist keine Haltung, das ist Physik.
Aus dieser Physik entsteht ein Markt, der in 15-Minuten-Scheiben handelt und keine Rücksicht nimmt. Genau dort läuft unsere Software.

Wir bewirtschaften heute 350 MWp Solar, 100 MWp Wind, 100 MWh Speicher, 12 MW Wasserstoff und über 40 HPC-Ladepunkte. Jede dieser Anlagen liefert Zeitreihen. Aus Zeitreihen werden Prognosen, aus Prognosen Fahrpläne, aus Fahrplänen Gebote an der Börse. Wenn ein Glied dieser Kette zwanzig Minuten zu spät ist, kostet das Geld. Nicht Story Points. Geld.

Wir haben die Plattform in wenigen Jahren von null auf 850 GWh gebracht. An einigen Stellen haben wir dabei bewusst pragmatisch gebaut, weil am Markt zu sein wichtiger war als sauber zu sein. Das war richtig.

Heute ist es das nicht mehr. Dieselben Abkürzungen, die uns schnell gemacht haben, bremsen uns inzwischen. Tabellen, die für Millionen Zeilen gedacht waren, halten Milliarden. Prozessketten, die früher jemand morgens von Hand angestoßen hat, laufen rund um die Uhr und dürfen nicht mehr ausfallen.
Wir suchen niemanden, der das verwaltet. Wir suchen jemanden, der es neu baut, während es läuft.
• Du entscheidest, wie unsere Systeme geschnitten sind. Nicht in einem Gremium, sondern indem Du den Vorschlag machst, ihn verteidigst und ihn anschließend umsetzt. Wer entscheidet, baut mit.

• PostgreSQL und TimescaleDB, Fahrpläne, Messwerte, Marktdaten. Schema, Partitionierung, Aggregation, Query-Pläne. Wenn eine Abfrage acht Sekunden braucht, ist das für uns ein Fehler und kein Feature.
• Prognose, Optimierung, Fahrplanübermittlung. Retry, Idempotenz, Alerting. Der Maßstab ist simpel: Was nachts schiefgeht, darf morgens niemand von Hand nacharbeiten müssen.

Netzbetreiber liefern Messwerte nach, korrigieren sie und schicken ein Jahr später erneut. Deine Läufe müssen das aushalten und beim zweiten Durchlauf dasselbe Ergebnis liefern wie beim ersten.
• PHP mit Laravel, React, PostgreSQL/TimescaleDB, Python. Tests, CI/CD und Monitoring gehören zur Umsetzung und nicht zu dem, was man danach noch macht.

We see the potential inside everything and everyone. Starting with you.

Orbem uses AI to industrialize MRI, delivering non-invasive insight into everything from fruits to eggs to the human body. We are transforming what is becoming the world's largest biological dataset into actionable intelligence to reduce waste, increase quality, and accelerate the shift toward a more sustainable and healthier future.

Headquartered and founded in Munich, Germany, with an office now in Houston, Texas, our world-class team is scaling inside-out technology to transform how humanity sees and understands biological matter.

Help us see what's possible. Join us.

Your Role

You will build Orbem's legal and compliance function largely from the ground up, at a pivotal moment. As we scale across Europe, into the US, and toward new geographies and verticals, legal and compliance touch nearly every part of the business — commercial contracts, corporate matters, employment, data protection, and product &
column2:

This is a role for a hands-on legal counsel who wants to build a function, not just run one — someone comfortable with ambiguity, who makes pragmatic, risk-balanced calls with incomplete information, and does the substantive legal work themselves while orchestrating a lean stack of external counsel.

A central part of the role is building Orbem's compliance function: a cross-functional, integrated approach to knowing and managing our risks — across intellectual property, product compliance, information security, data protection, and regulatory readiness. We treat compliance as an enabler of speed, not a brake on it — applying the right level of rigour for our stage and moment, so Orbem stays compliant and moves fast.

Die meisten Schülerjobs zeigen dir wenig: Regale einräumen, Spülmaschine, immer derselbe Handgriff.

Wir sind ein Beratungsunternehmen mit fast 15 Millionen Euro Umsatz, über 100 Mitarbeitern und dem Anspruch, Steuerberatung grundlegend zu modernisieren. Und auch als Schüler im Minijob bist du Teil davon — nicht am Rand, sondern mittendrin.

Du bist Schüler und suchst einen Nebenjob, der mehr ist als Taschengeld: Du packst mit an, damit der Laden läuft — in einem Umfeld, das digital arbeitet, in moderne Technik investiert und in dem du Dinge siehst und lernst, die dir in keinem anderen Schülerjob begegnen.

Was du bei uns nicht finden wirst

  • Kein Abstell-Job am Rand. Auch als Schüler im Minijob bist du Teil des Teams — mit echten Aufgaben, die das Unternehmen braucht.

  • Kein „wir geben dir Arbeit, wenn jemand frei ist, dich anzuleiten“-Setup. Du bekommst verbindliche Aufgabenpakete mit klarem Anleiter, nicht nur Lückenfüllung.

  • Kein verstaubtes Büro mit Papierbergen und Faxgerät. Wir investieren in moderne Technik und digitale Prozesse — du arbeitest mit Geräten und Tools, die dir in keinem anderen Schülerjob begegnen.

FAQ

1. Was ist Vogel — und wo arbeitet ihr?

Vogel ist eine der führenden Mittelstandsberatungen Deutschlands — Familienunternehmen seit 1959, aus Aalen — und baut daraus die führende Beratungsplattform für den Mittelstand. Wir wachsen an mehreren Standorten: in Aalen/Ostwürttemberg als gewachsenem Stammsitz und in München als neuem Hub. An beiden suchen wir quer durch die Funktionen — von Steuerberatung über Beratung bis zu den strategischen Teams, die die Plattform bauen.

2. Wie sind die Gehaltsbänder zu verstehen?

Bewusst breit — und an jeder Stelle ausgewiesen. Wir differenzieren nach Track Record und Marktwert, nicht nach Abschluss: knappe, stark gefragte Profile am oberen Ende, weniger knappe am unteren. Wir kalibrieren ausschließlich am Markt — zwei Menschen mit ähnlicher Erfahrung können bei uns unterschiedlich verdienen.

3. Wie viel — und wie — wird bei Vogel gearbeitet?

Gemessen wird an dem, was du bewegst, nicht an Stunden. Ehrlich ist aber auch: Wer 9-to-5 sucht, ist bei uns nicht die erste Adresse. Wir suchen Menschen, die aus eigenem Antrieb intensiv arbeiten, weil die Aufgaben es wert sind. Wie du deine Zeit verteilst, ist weitgehend deine Sache. Was wir teilen: Wir arbeiten präsent zusammen — Kultur, Sparring und die besten Ideen entstehen in der täglichen Nähe. Wir sind keine Remote-Company und haben keine großen Home-Office-Policies
column6:
einzelne Remote-Tage sind kein Problem.

4. Wie läuft die Bewerbung?

Schlank, schnell, transparent — und nach Profil gestaffelt. Für Einstiegsrollen (Praktikum, Werkstudium, Berufseinstieg) genügen in der Regel zwei Gespräche und eine kurze Arbeitsprobe
column7:

5. Wie funktioniert die variable Vergütung?

Quartalsweise an Leistung gekoppelt, qualitativ bewertet. Die Skala steigt mit dem Level: bis 20 % Associate, 27,5 % Manager, 35 % Senior Manager, 42,5 % Director, 50 % VP. Erwartungswert bei guter Leistung — du erfüllst die Anforderungen, setzt eigene Akzente, bestehst den Keeper Test — liegt bei rund 50 % des Maximums
column8:

6. Wie entwickle ich mich — welche Karrierewege gibt es?

Zwei aktive Wege: Mastery (fachliche Tiefe, Expertenlaufbahn) und Pioneer (Führung, Management). Die Richtung wählst du nach dem Onboarding, meist in Jahr 1–3. Berufseinstieg ist kein Sonderweg, sondern der frühe Teil derselben Strecke — vom Werkstudenten oder Praktikanten zum Associate, für die Besten ohne erneutes Bewerbungsverfahren.

What We’re Building

Cello helps businesses turn their users into their best acquisition channel. Our product is the easiest way to embed user and partner referrals directly into the products you love to use. With just a few lines of code, a company is set up for hyper growth that runs on autopilot instead of spending money on ads.

Teams at Bolt, Miro, Typeform, VEED, and Descript already run their referral programs on Cello. which is proof that word-of-mouth can be engineered as a real growth channel, not being a nice to have.

We're a small, remote-first team that builds infrastructure that lives in other people's products. That means our bar for craft and attention to detail is exceptionally high. Our UI has to feel native inside other people's products that we don't control, our components have to hold up wildly across different use cases, and our decisions get scrutinized by the world's best growth, design and engineering teams. So in addition to caring deeply about how things look and feel, we need people who can think in systems, tracing how a decision plays out across different user segments and across levels of the product.

The Role

We're looking for a Senior Product Designer to work closely with our founding designer, product and engineering teams on the core Cello experience. You'll be involved in every aspect of the product design cycle and expected to take ownership of the work end-to-end.

This role is fully remote but your work schedule needs to overlap comfortably with a European work day. We're an async-first culture that values deep focused work, but we still make time to get together in person at regular team off-sites.

  • Partner directly with our founding designer, product and engineering teams to take projects on our roadmap from rough problem to shipped solution.

  • Look for opportunities to improve our existing product areas. Sometimes that's a full rethink of how something works, others itʼs fixing smaller quality issues you pick up in the product.

  • Help define and improve our evolving design system.

  • Bring our brand to life across marketing, social and launch content.

  • Design mockups and prototypes in low and high fidelity to communicate ideas and how things might work.

  • Be part of and contribute to a growing design culture that's still taking shape.

  • Sweat the details that make embedded UI feel trustworthy.

  • Solid and proven software design experience

  • Youʼve ideally designed software for SaaS businesses, but we also love to see range in the type of products youʼve worked on.

  • Breadth of craft: Youʼre able to comfortably flex across visual design, product thinking, brand, and interaction design.

  • Systems thinking: you can design components and patterns while thinking about how they fit into the broader system, but you also know when to push past convention and innovate.

  • Courage to challenge ideas, try new things and push a product direction forward.

Vogel ist eine der führenden Mittelstandsberatungen Deutschlands — Familienunternehmen seit 1959, aus Aalen — und baut daraus die führende Beratungsplattform für den Mittelstand. Wir wachsen an mehreren Standorten: in Aalen/Ostwürttemberg als gewachsenem Stammsitz und in München als neuem Hub. Bewusst breit — und an jeder Stelle ausgewiesen. Wir differenzieren nach Track Record und Marktwert, nicht nach Abschluss: knappe, stark gefragte Profile am oberen Ende, weniger knappe am unteren. Gemessen wird an dem, was du bewegst, nicht an Stunden. Ehrlich ist aber auch: Wer 9-to-5 sucht, ist bei uns nicht die erste Adresse. product-manager-courier-delivery-experience-berlin-471911,Wolt - English,"Product Manager, Courier Delivery Experience","

About Wolt

At Wolt, we create technology that brings joy, simplicity and earnings to the neighborhoods of the world. In 2014 we started with delivery of restaurant food. Now we're building the delivery of (almost) everything and you'll find us in over 500 cities in 30 countries around the world. In 2022 we joined forces with DoorDash and together we keep on dreaming big and expanding across the globe.

Working at Wolt isn't always easy, but it's definitely exciting. Here you'll learn more, build more, and ship more than in most other companies. You'll be challenged a lot, but also have a lot of fun on the way. So, if you're a self-starter with drive and entrepreneurial spirit, this could be the ride of your life.

We seek a Product Manager to join our Courier and Delivery Experience (CDX) team. This role will focus on ensuring world-class courier and consumer delivery experiences while continually evolving the delivery process with a future-oriented mindset. The Courier and Delivery Experience team owns the experiences that elevate every Wolt delivery, from the moment a courier opens the app to every order they accept, all the way to dropping an order off at the customer's doorstep. The team sits at the intersection of a multi-sided marketplace product, real-world operations, and safety, and the work directly moves how reliable Wolt feels to consumers and how satisfied our couriers are when delivering.

You will play a crucial role in shaping the courier experience, ensuring that our couriers feel valued and supported while enhancing the efficiency of deliveries. By blending operational expertise with a deep understanding of courier needs, you will improve the user journey from onboarding couriers to completing deliveries. From designing new features that boost courier satisfaction to refining delivery processes, your work will contribute to key metrics across courier engagement, performance, and satisfaction. You will also be influential in shaping the evolution of the live delivery experience for our courier partners, the merchant courier interaction at pickup and the consumer courier interaction at the doorstep via the Courier app surfaces.

The ideal candidate will have an exceptional track record in product management, with proven success in working with cross-functional teams across engineering, design, product, and operations. You will define the vision and roadmap for courier and delivery experiences across multiple projects. Working in partnership with business stakeholders, you will also collaborate on cross-team initiatives, contributing to the broader business strategy while ensuring a deep understanding of the courier experience.
Join us in shaping the future of delivery, where every delivery is an opportunity for delight and loyalty.
You could come to this role from various backgrounds, but ideally, you bring:
• Several years of experience in product management, specializing in consumer-facing products
• Expertise in developing user-centric products, with the ability to address complex user experience-related challenges.
• Demonstrated expertise in supporting cross-functional teams and fostering operational excellence in fast-paced, high-demand industries.
• Proven track record in building products influencing cross-functional teams, including engineering, data, design, and operations.
• High ownership and collaborative capabilities, making thoughtful decisions, and focusing on product details to ensure execution aligns with the vision.
• Strong ability to define, execute, and measure meaningful OKRs, ensuring alignment with company-wide goals and fostering bottom-up alignment from your team.
• Ability to focus on the bigger picture, creating solutions that benefit couriers, operations, and customer experiences across the organization.
• Excellent stakeholder management skills, able to work effectively with diverse internal teams and external partners, while confidently engaging with leadership in a high-visibility role
The position will be filled as soon as we find the right person, so make sure to apply as soon as you realize you really, really want to join us!

The compensation will be a negotiable combination of monthly pay and DoorDash RSUs. The latter makes it exceptionally easy to be excited about our company growing and doing well, as you'll own a piece of the pie.
Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion

We're committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That's why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel.

Frontend platform architecture

  • Strengthen platform contracts such as plugin systems, extension points, and frontend developer experience.

Canvas, collaboration, and real-time systems

  • Build and improve real-time collaboration capabilities using approaches such as WebSockets, CRDTs, or multiplayer synchronization patterns.

  • Design frontend systems with correctness, accessibility, and user experience in mind, especially for complex interactive workflows.

Performance and rendering foundations

  • Use performance measurement, profiling, and optimization techniques to identify bottlenecks and improve user experience.

  • Contribute to web worker orchestration and other frontend infrastructure that helps n8n scale to more complex use cases.

Technical contribution and collaboration

Must-haves

  • 🤝 Collaboration: You communicate clearly, work cross-functionally, and enjoy enabling other engineers rather than building in isolation.

  • 🧹 Pragmatic engineering: You’re excited by refactoring, modularization, tech debt reduction, and improving existing systems over time.

Nice-to-haves

Apply now — and help us build the future of automation.

Wir suchen Dich

Du willst Marketing nicht nur in der Vorlesung hören, sondern wirklich machen?
Du hast Lust, in Zahlen einzutauchen, kreativ zu werden und im Team Kampagnen aufzubauen, die vor allem unsere DACH-Crowd aktivieren? Dann passt du ziemlich gut zu uns.
Bei Invesdor, Europas führender Impact-Investmentplattform, verbinden wir Rendite mit Wirkung. Über unsere Plattform investieren Menschen in Unternehmen, die die Welt ein Stück besser machen wollen – von erneuerbaren Energien bis hin zu MedTech und EdTech.
